questions.prompt:
Let \(R\) be enclosed by
\[
y=\tan^2x,\qquad y=\frac12\sec^2x,\qquad x=0.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.answer:
The curves meet at \(x=\pi/4\). Hence
\[
A=\int_0^{\pi/4}\left(\frac12\sec^2x-\tan^2x\right)dx=\boxed{\frac\pi4-\frac12}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
f(x)=2\ln(x^2+3)-x,\qquad -3\le x\le5.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find each relative maximum and relative minimum \(x\)-coordinate.
parts.answer:
\[
f'(x)=-\frac{(x-1)(x-3)}{x^2+3}.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{x=1}\) is a relative minimum and \(\boxed{x=3}\) is a relative maximum.

questions.prompt: A trough is \(5\) feet long. Each vertical cross section is an inverted isosceles triangle with base \(2\) feet and height \(3\) feet. Water is siphoned out at \(2\) cubic feet per minute.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the volume when full.
parts.answer: Full cross-sectional area is \(3\) square feet, so \(\boxed{V=15\text{ ft}^3}\).

parts.prompt: Find \(dh/dt\) when the trough is one-quarter full by volume.
parts.answer:
Similarity gives width \(2h/3\), so \(V=5h^2/3\). At quarter volume, \(h=3/2\). Since \(dV/dt=-2\),

\]

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)<1\) and \(f'(x)<0\) for all real \(x\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Suppose \(f(b)=0\) and \(a<b<c\). Write an integral expression for the area bounded by the graph, \(x=a\), \(x=c\), and the \(x\)-axis.
parts.answer:
Since \(f\) is decreasing, it is positive left of \(b\) and negative right of \(b\). The area is
\[
\boxed{\int_a^b f(x)\,dx-\int_b^c f(x)\,dx}.
\]

parts.answer:

questions.prompt:
Let \(R\) be the first-quadrant region enclosed by
\[
x^2-y^2=9,\qquad y=0,\qquad x=5.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the volume when \(R\) is revolved about the \(x\)-axis.
parts.answer:
Here \(y^2=x^2-9\) for \(3\le x\le5\). Thus
\[
V=\pi\int_3^5(x^2-9)dx=\boxed{\frac{44\pi}{3}}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let \(f\) be differentiable for all real \(x\) and suppose
\[
f'(x)=ax^2+bx,\qquad f'(1)=6,\qquad f''(1)=18,\qquad \int_1^2f(x)\,dx=18.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(f(x)\).
parts.answer:
From \(a+b=6\) and \(2a+b=18\), \(a=12,b=-6\). Hence
\[
f(x)=4x^3-3x^2+C.
\]
The integral condition gives \(8+C=18\), so
\[
\boxed{f(x)=4x^3-3x^2+10}.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.answer:

questions.prompt:
Let \(R\) be enclosed by
\[
y=e^x,\qquad y=(x-1)^2,\qquad x=1.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.answer:
The curves meet at \(x=0\). Thus
\[
A=\int_0^1\left(e^x-(x-1)^2\right)dx=\boxed{e-\frac43}.
\]

questions.prompt:
The radius of a sphere increases at the constant rate
\[
\frac{dr}{dt}=0.04\text{ cm/s},\qquad V=\frac43\pi r^3.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: When \(r=10\), find \(dV/dt\).
parts.answer:
\[
\frac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}=\boxed{16\pi\text{ cm}^3/\text{s}}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: When \(V=36\pi\), find the rate of change of the area of a central cross section.
parts.answer:
Then \(r=3\). Since \(A=\pi r^2\),
\[
\boxed{\frac{dA}{dt}=2\pi(3)(0.04)=\frac{6\pi}{25}\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}}.
\]

parts.prompt: When the volume and radius increase at the same numerical rate, find \(r\).
parts.answer:
Set \(dV/dt=dr/dt\) and cancel the positive \(dr/dt\):
\[
4\pi r^2=1,\qquad \boxed{r=\frac1{2\sqrt\pi}\text{ cm}}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
f(x)=\sin^2x-\sin x,\qquad 0\le x\le\frac{3\pi}{2}.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the \(x\)-intercepts.
parts.answer:
\[
\sin x(\sin x-1)=0,
\]
so \(\boxed{x=0,\pi/2,\pi}\).

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
f(x)=\frac{ax+b}{x^2-c}.
\]
Suppose the graph is symmetric about the \(y\)-axis, \(\lim_{x\to2^+}f(x)=+\infty\), and \(f'(1)=-2\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Determine \(a,b,c\).
parts.answer:
Even symmetry forces \(a=0\). The vertical blow-up at \(x=2\) gives \(c=4\) and requires \(b>0\). Since
\[
f'(x)=-\frac{2bx}{(x^2-4)^2},
\]
evaluating at \(1\) gives \(-2b/9=-2\), so \(\boxed{a=0,b=9,c=4}\).

questions.prompt:
Let \(f\) be defined for all real \(x\) and satisfy
\[
f''(x)=24x-18,\qquad f'(1)=-6,\qquad f(2)=0.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find every \(x\) for which the tangent line to the graph of \(f\) is horizontal.
parts.answer:
Integrating once,
\[
f'(x)=12x^2-18x+C.
\]
The condition \(f'(1)=-6\) gives \(C=0\). Thus
\[
f'(x)=6x(2x-3),
\]
so the horizontal tangents occur at
\[
\boxed{x=0\quad\text{and}\quad x=\frac32}.
\]

\[
y=1+\sin(\pi x)\qquad\text{and}\qquad y=x^2
\]

A=\int_0^1\bigl(1+\sin(\pi x)-x^2\bigr)\,dx
=\boxed{\frac23+\frac2\pi}.
\]

questions.prompt: The source table describes an even continuous function on \([-3,3]\), together with the signs of \(f\), \(f'\), and \(f''\) on the positive half of the interval.

parts.label: (a)

questions.prompt: A tightrope is 30 feet above the ground between two buildings 50 feet apart. A spotlight is 70 feet above point A. A walker moves from A toward B at 2 feet per second.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: How fast is the shadow of the walker's feet moving along the ground when the walker is midway between the buildings?
parts.answer:
Let \(x\) be the walker's horizontal distance from A and \(s\) the ground-shadow distance. Similar triangles give
\[
\frac{s}{70}=\frac{x}{40},
\qquad s=\frac74x.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{\frac{ds}{dt}=\frac72\text{ ft/s}}.
\]

questions.prompt:

parts.prompt: Find the minimum acceleration.
parts.answer:

a(t)=6t-12.
\]

questions.prompt:
Consider the curve
\[
y+\cos y=x+1,
\qquad 0\le y\le2\pi.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(dy/dx\) in terms of \(y\).
parts.answer:
Implicit differentiation gives
\[
(1-\sin y)\frac{dy}{dx}=1,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac1{1-\sin y}}.
\]

\qquad g(x)=kx,

Thus \(x=-1\) and

questions.prompt: The volume of a sphere increases at a rate proportional to the reciprocal of its radius. At \(t=0\), the radius is 1, and at \(t=15\), the radius is 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the radius as a function of time.
parts.answer:
With \(V=\frac43\pi r^3\) and \(dV/dt=K/r\),
\[
4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac Kr.
\]
Integration gives \(r^4=At+1\). Since \(r(15)=2\), \(A=1\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{r(t)=(t+1)^{1/4}}.
\]

parts.answer:
A factor of 27 in volume means a factor of 3 in radius. Set \(r=3\):

3^4=t+1.
\]
Thus

\boxed{t=80}.

questions.prompt:
Consider the curve
\[
y^2=x+4
\]
and the chord joining \(A(-4,0)\) to \(B(0,2)\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the point on the curve where the tangent is parallel to the chord.
parts.answer:
The chord slope is \(1/2\). Since
\[
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac1{2y},
\]
parallelism requires \(y=1\), giving \(x=-3\). Thus
\[
\boxed{(-3,1)}.
\]

The upper branch is \(y=\sqrt{x+4}\) and the chord is \(y=(x+4)/2\). Therefore
\[
A=\int_{-4}^0\left(\sqrt{x+4}-\frac{x+4}{2}\right)dx
=\boxed{\frac43}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
f(x)=\ln(2+\sin x),
\qquad \pi\le x\le2\pi.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the absolute maximum and minimum values.
parts.answer:
The critical point in the interval is \(x=3\pi/2\). At the endpoints, \(f=\ln2\), while at \(3\pi/2\), \(f=0\). Hence
\[
\boxed{f_{\max}=\ln2},
\qquad
\boxed{f_{\min}=0}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Consider the curve
\[
x^2+xy+y^2=27.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the slope at a general point \((x,y)\).
parts.answer:
Implicit differentiation gives
\[
\boxed{\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{2x+y}{x+2y}}.
\]

questions.prompt: A circle is inscribed in a square. The circle circumference increases at 6 inches per second, and the square expands to remain tangent.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the rate at which the square perimeter increases.
parts.answer:
Since \(C=2\pi r\),
\[
\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac3\pi.
\]
The square side is \(2r\), so its perimeter is \(8r\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac{dP}{dt}=\frac{24}{\pi}\text{ in/s}}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: When the circle area is 25 square inches, find the rate of increase of the area between the square and circle.
parts.answer:
The area difference is
\[
D=(4-\pi)r^2.
\]
When \(\pi r^2=25\), \(r=5/\sqrt\pi\). Thus
\[
\boxed{\frac{dD}{dt}=\frac{30(4-\pi)}{\pi\sqrt\pi}\text{ in}^2/\text{s}}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
F(x)=\int_0^x\sin(t^2)\,dt,
\qquad 0\le x\le3.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use the Trapezoidal Rule with four equal subdivisions of \([0,1]\) to approximate \(F(1)\).
parts.answer:
With \(\Delta x=1/4\),
\[
F(1)\approx\frac18\left[\sin0+2\sin\frac1{16}+2\sin\frac14+2\sin\frac9{16}+\sin1\right]
\approx\boxed{0.316}.
\]

parts.prompt: On what intervals is \(F\) increasing?
parts.answer:
By the Fundamental Theorem,
\[
F'(x)=\sin(x^2).
\]
On \(0<x<3\), this is positive for
\[
\boxed{(0,\sqrt\pi)\cup(\sqrt{2\pi},3)}.
\]

questions.prompt:
A particle moves on the \(y\)-axis with
\[
v(t)=t\cos t,
\qquad t\ge0,
\qquad y(0)=3.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For \(0<t<5\), when is the particle moving upward?
parts.answer:

\[
\boxed{(0,\pi/2)\cup(3\pi/2,5)}.
\]

questions.prompt:
The regions \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are enclosed by
\[
f(x)=x^2
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
g(x)=2^x.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the three points of intersection.
parts.answer:
The positive intersections are \((2,4)\) and \((4,16)\). The negative intersection is numerical:
\[
x\approx-0.766665,
\qquad y\approx0.587775.
\]
Thus the three points are approximately
\[
\boxed{(-0.767,0.588),\ (2,4),\ (4,16)}.
\]

questions.prompt: Water drains from a conical tank of height 12 feet and diameter 8 feet into a cylindrical tank whose base area is \(400\pi\) square feet. The conical water depth satisfies \(dh/dt=h-12\) feet per minute.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express the conical water volume as a function of \(h\).
parts.answer:
Similarity gives \(r/h=4/12=1/3\). Hence
\[
\boxed{V(h)=\frac{\pi h^3}{27}}.
\]

parts.prompt: Find \(dV/dt\) when \(h=3\).
parts.answer:

\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{\pi h^2}{9}\frac{dh}{dt}.

\boxed{\frac{dV}{dt}=-9\pi\text{ ft}^3/\text{min}}.
\]

The cylinder gains water at \(9\pi\) cubic feet per minute. Since \(W=400\pi y\),

questions.prompt: For \(b>0\), let \(f(x)=x+b\sin x\) on \([-2\pi,2\pi]\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Sketch \(y=x+\sin x\) and \(y=x+3\sin x\).
parts.answer: Both graphs oscillate about the line \(y=x\). The first is nondecreasing with horizontal tangencies at odd multiples of \(\pi\); the second has alternating local extrema because \(1+3\cos x\) changes sign.
